about: The line of promise from Adam to Jesus, in segments with their sources. Names follow the ESV spellings as remembered at seeding (14 November 2026); check spelling against the text before printing. Seeded by Barnabas.

segments.title: Adam to Noah
segments.note: Ten generations before the flood. Enoch 'walked with God, and he was not, for God took him' (Genesis 5:24).

segments.title: Shem to Abraham
segments.note: Luke 3:36 adds a Cainan between Arpachshad and Shelah, as the Greek Old Testament does. Eber may lie behind the word 'Hebrew'.

segments.title: Abraham to David
segments.note: Matthew names four women in the line (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Uriah's wife), each with an unlikely story. Grace runs through the family tree.

segments.title: David to the exile: the kings (Matthew)
segments.note: Matthew skips Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah between Joram and Uzziah, to shape three sets of fourteen (Matthew 1:17). Jehoiachin is the king named on the Babylonian ration tablets in the timeline.

segments.title: The exile to Jesus (Matthew)
segments.note: Zerubbabel led the first return from Babylon (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1). After him, the names appear only in Matthew.

segments.title: Luke's line: through Nathan
segments.note: Luke traces the line back through David's son Nathan, not Solomon, and goes on to Adam, 'the son of God' (3:38). Why Matthew and Luke differ is DISPUTED: Matthew may give the legal royal line through Joseph, and Luke Mary's line or Joseph's natural line. Both agree that Jesus is the son of David and the son of Abraham.
